Command: Do not extinguish the altar fire
Summary: The command: Do not extinguish the altar fire (Leviticus 6:12). The fire on the altar was never to go out; wood was laid on it every morning.
Commandment: Do not extinguish the altar fire.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: The fire on the altar was never to go out, and wood was laid on it every morning — a ceremonial law of tending. Its goal was to keep the God-kindled fire alive, so the altar was never cold and the offerings never waited on a dead flame. The evil was neglect: letting the heart of Israel's worship go out through carelessness. It restrained that by making the fire a daily charge — someone tended it every morning, without fail.
